chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah told me, Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar told me, from his brother, from Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in a lengthy tradition,

at its end that the doors of heaven are opened in Ramadan, the devils are shackled, and the deeds of the believers are accepted. What an excellent month, the month of Ramadan; it was called al-Marzooq during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَبْوَابَ السَّمَاءِ: The doors of heaven, symbolizing increased divine grace and acceptance of prayers.
key_terms.أَعْمَالُ الْمُؤْمِنِینَ: The deeds/actions of the believers, which are accepted by God during this sacred time.
key_terms.الْمَرْزُوقَ: Al-Marzooq, a title for Ramadan meaning 'the one who is provided for' or 'the month of sustenance/bounties.'
key_terms.تُصَفَّدُ الشَّیَاطِینُ: The devils are shackled/chained, indicating a reduction in their influence over humans during this month.
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
key_terms.رَمَضَان: Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting and spiritual elevation.

ai.seo_question: What are the special virtues and titles of the month of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* underscores the metaphysical transformation of Ramadan, where divine mercy is amplified through the opening of the gates of heaven and the chaining of devils, facilitating the acceptance of believers' deeds. The specific designation of the month as 'al-Marzooq' (the Sustained One) highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on Ramadan as a unique period of divine provision and spiritual nourishment, distinct from other months. This context reinforces the month's role not merely as a time of fasting, but as a cosmic opportunity for spiritual elevation and divine grace.
